title: The Prophet at home
carry: the best of you is best to family
tomorrow: nine o'clock: dad's knee exercises, or the study group. which door?

segments.voice: Yesterday, provision is written: tie the camel, then trust. That closed work and money. The next stretch is family, and it starts at the sink.

A sink full of dishes. A tired voice, a sharp one back, and a door that closes a little harder than it needed to. Every home has a sound like that. So what did the Prophet ﷺ do at home? Someone once asked his wife 'A'isha exactly that. Her answer, kept in Sahih al-Bukhari, is so plain it almost surprises: he was in the service of his family, and when the time for prayer came, he went out to pray.
screen: `A SINK, A SHARP WORD, A DOOR.` → `WHAT DID HE DO AT HOME?` → `IN THE SERVICE OF HIS FAMILY.`

segments.voice: Another report fills in the picture with things you could hear and touch. 'A'isha said he mended his own sandal and sewed his own clothes, and worked around the house the way anyone does. Thread pulled through cloth. The tap of a sandal being fixed. That's the sound of mercy at home in these reports: not a speech, small work with the hands. And notice the order in her first answer: the family, and then, when the call came, the prayer. Neither cancels the other. The Qur'an names what a home stands on. In Pickthall's words, God "ordained between you love and mercy." Then there's a scene with a grandchild. The Prophet kissed his grandson al-Hasan, and a visiting man said he had never kissed any of his own children. The Prophet looked at him and said: whoever shows no mercy is shown no mercy. A hadith in Tirmidhi gathers it all up: the best of you is the best to his family. Notice where that puts the test. Not in the masjid, not at work. At the sink, with the people who see you tired. One to tell someone tonight: the Messenger of God sewed his own clothes.
screen: `HE MENDED HIS OWN SANDAL.` · `LOVE AND MERCY BETWEEN YOU.` · `A KISS FOR AL-HASAN.` · `THE BEST TO HIS FAMILY.` · then, large: `MERCY AT HOME.`

segments.voice: Find one small thing at home that needs your hands: a shirt to fold, a cup to wash, a pair of shoes to straighten. Do it slowly, and listen while you work, to the water, the fabric, the small sounds of a house. Let it be for the people you live with, even if nobody notices.
screen: `ONE SMALL THING, BY HAND.` · `LISTEN WHILE YOU WORK.`

segments.voice: Mercy at home: rahma, lived in small work for the people you live with. He served his family, then went out to pray.
Keep this close: the best of you is the best to family, in the small work nobody claps for. Family and friendship, day one.

fork.setup: your older brother gets home from a long shift and snaps at you about the noise. you're tired too. what fits the Prophet at home?
options: snap back; mercy doesn't mean letting people be rude to you.
turn it down, make him a plate, and talk about it later.
ignore him for the night; he'll get over it by morning.
fork.reveal: the reports show mercy at home as small service, not a speech. the talk can come later; the plate comes first.

chat.says: dad left his dishes again 'cause knee. i said something mean. now he's sulking. but i'm right??
options: Maybe right, still mean. Do the dishes beside him. Mercy at home is small work.
You're right, so wait it out. He's the parent; he should apologize first.

chat.meaning: 'A'isha said the Prophet served his family at home, and he said the best of you is the best to family. Mercy at home lives in small work, even on the days you're right.
